analysis.investment_thesis: Nukleus Office fails the Magic Formula on both axes: a P/E of 37 implies an earnings yield near 2.7% (far below my 12% threshold) while ROE of 0.10% signals capital is generating essentially no return. A capital-intensive co-working lessor priced like a growth story is the opposite of "cheap and good."
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 69.91% indicates aligned skin-in-the-game
Operates in a structurally growing flexible-workspace category in Delhi NCR
Small ₹85 Cr base could allow rapid scaling if unit economics turn
key_risks: ROE of 0.10% — capital is effectively earning nothing
P/E 37 with negligible profitability = earnings yield ~2.7%, deeply overvalued
Co-working is capex/lease-heavy with thin margins and operating-leverage downside
red_flags: Recent incorporation (Dec 2019) — no multi-year track record of high ROIC
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Magic Formula lens, this is a near-textbook reject. Earnings yield, approximated by 1/P/E, sits at ~2.7% — investors are paying ₹37 for ₹1 of earnings in a business where each rupee of equity is producing one-tenth of a paisa of profit. The combination of a rich multiple AND a near-zero return on capital means the stock fails BOTH screens simultaneously, which is the worst quadrant in my framework.

Structurally, co-working is a tough business model: long-duration lease liabilities funded by short-duration member contracts, heavy fit-out capex, and limited pricing power versus landlords. Even with a tailwind in flexible workspace demand and a committed 69.91% promoter, the unit economics need to inflect dramatically before ROIC could reach the 20%+ I require. Until EBIT/EV moves above 12% and ROIC sustainably crosses 20%, this is a clear avoid.
